title: Glen Scrivener vs Michael Shermer || EPIC DEBATE
proposedQuestion: Can we be good without God?

duplicateScreening.searched: Current production data, standalone records, video URLs and speaker/motion metadata; original upload ID checked separately.

sourceEvidence.coverage: Complete opening through closing; final rolling caption overlaps nominal duration by approximately 1.52 seconds.
sourceEvidence.limitations: Automatic captions contain recognition errors. Speaker boundaries and timing are caption-based estimates, not independent audio-confirmed timings.

screeningIntervals.classificationRationale: Vitale contrasts reciprocal self-interest with his stated conception of genuine morality as recognition of another person’s inherent worth.
Vitale uses a six-finger counterfactual to challenge whether evolved moral rules can be objective and absolute.
Vitale develops the premise that equal human value requires something equally true of every person, then asks both speakers to identify it.
Vitale contrasts cognitively limited humans and infants with cognitively superior animals to challenge the boundary of the moral community.
Vitale asks how cultural and evolutionary moral development can be known to track independently existing moral truth.
Vitale contrasts Shermer’s concession about limits of science with the apparent need for an objectively correct answer to abortion and other moral disputes.

timingCalculation.method: Sum six non-overlapping clearly host-attributed caption intervals. Mixed initial caption cues are omitted from four intervals. The entire video is used only as a generous denominator for screening, not as a frozen assessment window. Other host interventions and all participant response time are omitted from this timing calculation.
timingCalculation.precisionWarning: The numerical result is exact arithmetic on caption boundaries, not exact measurement of spoken advocacy duration.

requirements: Host substantive advocacy must occupy at most 5% of the assessed window.
Every host argument must merely duplicate or prompt a line independently developed by a primary speaker.
Directly dependent replies must also be excluded under the ordinary scope exception.

decisionRationale: Caption-based screening places six substantive interventions above 5% even against the full recording; a genuine assessed window would be shorter.
The moderator supplies reasoning and counterexamples rather than only directing turns.
Independent duplication by a primary speaker is not established for every intervention, particularly the question of how evolved beliefs track independently existing moral truth.
No attempt was made to force eligibility by relabeling the moderator as a teammate, dropping his material, or silently retaining directly dependent replies.

neededUserDecision.concreteProposedException: Assess only Michael Shermer and Glen Scrivener across the full substantive discussion. Retain moderator interventions as context and evaluate the primary speakers’ own substantive replies. Attribute no moderator argument to either primary speaker, give the moderator no score, account for unequal questioning in move selection, and clearly disclose the expanded moderator participation. This would require a separately authorized source-scope rule; it is not permitted by the current 5% exclusion rule.
